title: fix(app-shell): a position approver is read through the spec's registry binding (objectui#7611 Q3b)
body:
Part of #7611
Clause-②: no. No published acceptance set widens and no public surface grows: no authoring face, zod face or `objectui validate` input is touched, and none of the touched modules is re-exported from `@object-ui/app-shell`'s index. The one reader that now keeps more is the designer's reading of the server-published `xRef.sources`, a renderer input rather than an accepted-metadata set.

Q3b of objectstack-ai/objectstack#22865, ruled B (comment 6115690641; pointer on #7611, comment 6115700897). The approval read side lists positions for a `{ source: 'registry', type }` approver binding from the registry and stores the name only. Item 3a (the decision-output position picker, objectui#12152) is not touched: none of its files are in this diff. #7611 remains open for its other parts.

## What changes

- **`approverValueSources` (new, `packages/app-shell/src/utils`).** The spec's `APPROVER_VALUE_SOURCES` as published, typed so the registry member objectstack#22710 added can be tested for. The installed spec 17.7.0 predates that member, so the type is widened here and marked **LOOSENED FOR SPEC 17, remove at spec 18**. A pin (`approverValueSources.test.ts`, "the installed spec binds nothing to the registry yet") turns red on the bump to say so. Which kinds are registry-bound is read off the binding; nothing in the diff lists `position` as a registry kind.
- **The approval panel and the override dialog** (`approverIdentity`, `useApproverDirectory`). A reference whose kind is registry-bound carries a machine name: it is prettified rather than truncated, it is handed to the directory, and its label comes from the registry item read through the console's metadata store (`ensureType(TYPE)`, the `GET /api/v1/meta/TYPE` read the Approval Center and item 3a already make). Staffing still reads `sys_user_position` by name. `DeclaredActionsBar` picks this up without an edit.
- **The flow designer's approver Value cell** (`json-schema-to-fields`, `flow-node-config`, `FlowReferenceField`). A published `registry` source is kept instead of dropped. A kind bound that way renders a select over that metadata type's items (the designer's metadata client, `GET /api/v1/meta/TYPE`) and commits the item's `name`. It keeps the pencil toggle for manual entry, flags a stored name the registry does not list as `(not found)`, and leaves the text box when the registry lists nothing. With no published source, the fallback is derived from the bundled spec in the same way as the record lookup table.
- **The record arm is unchanged.** A `data` binding (`user`, `team`, `department`, and `position` under the installed spec) renders the same record lookup and resolves its label from the same directory object.
- One i18n key (`engine.inspector.reference.pickFromRegistry`, en and zh). The app-shell README and the flow-designer guide each gain one paragraph.

## Measured in a browser (both symptoms reproduced on base first)

Setup: objectstack `main` `7dbb89dc5`, `examples/app-showcase` booted with `objectstack dev --seed-admin --fresh` (closure build exit 0). `GET /api/v1/meta/position` serves 16 positions; `GET /api/v1/data/sys_position` answers `"records":[]`. Each console was `vite build` plus `vite preview` with the `/api` proxy pointed at that server, built two ways:

- **injected**, with `OBJECTSTACK_SPEC_DIST` set to objectstack main's `packages/spec`, the way objectstack builds the console it ships. Bundle check: the registry spelling of the position binding appears 5 times, and the vendored spelling (`source` `record`, object `sys_position`) appears 0 times;
- **vendored**, objectui's own spec 17.7.0.

A probe flow, `q3b_position_probe`, was saved with `PUT /api/v1/meta/flow/q3b_position_probe`. It triggers on an account update and has one approval node whose approvers are position `manager` (held by the admin) and position `field_ops_delegate` (held by nobody), with `unanimous` behaviour. Updating Acme Retail opened a request whose `pending_approvers` is the admin's id and `position:field_ops_delegate`.

| console | record page, Approvals tab, "Waiting on" | flow designer, Seat review, approver Value |
|---|---|---|
| base `d2500d8be`, injected | `Dev Admin`, `positi…gate` (title `position:field_ops_delegate`); no request to `/meta/position` or `/data/sys_position` | two plain text inputs (`manager`, `field_ops_delegate`) with no datalist, and no candidate request |
| base `d2500d8be`, vendored | `Field Ops Delegate (no current holder)`; reads `GET /data/sys_position` (empty) | a `sys_position` record lookup that hydrates nothing, so both stored names render blank (placeholder shown); two `GET /data/sys_position` reads |
| branch, injected | `Field Ops Delegate Admin (no current holder)`, the registry label; `GET /api/v1/meta/position` only | two registry selects showing `Project Manager (manager)` and `Field Ops Delegate Admin (field_ops_delegate)`; `GET /api/v1/meta/position` only |
| branch, vendored | unchanged from base vendored (the record arm under spec 17.7.0) | two registry selects, the same as injected (the published source wins) |

Picking on the branch (injected): the select offers all 16 positions, labelled `LABEL (name)`. Choosing `Operations (ops)` made the designer's save send `"approvers":[{"type":"position","value":"ops"},{"type":"position","value":"field_ops_delegate"}]`, so the name is the only thing stored.

## Tests (head `61a2d3ed0`)

- New pins, 4 files and 25 tests, one pin per arm: `approverValueSources.test.ts`, `approverIdentity.registryBinding-7611.test.tsx` (mocks the spec into the injected shape), `FlowReferenceField.registrySource-7611.test.tsx` and `FlowReferenceField.injectedRegistryBinding-7611.test.tsx` (the second mocks the spec into the injected shape).
- Touched suites plus their consumers: 75 files (every `FlowReferenceField*`, `json-schema-to-fields*`, `flow-node-config*`, `FlowNodeInspector*`, `approver*`, `useApproverDirectory*`, `RecordApprovalsPanel*`, `DeclaredActionsBar*`, `ApprovalsInboxPage*`, `approvalsApi*` test, plus the four other tests that import a touched module). Result: `Test Files 75 passed (75)`, `Tests 824 passed | 1 skipped (825)`.
- `pnpm --filter @object-ui/app-shell type-check` (both `tsc` passes) exit 0, after building the `@object-ui/app-shell^...` closure (28/28 tasks). The test program's file list contains all four new test files.
- Gates, exit 0: `check:i18n-keys`, `check:i18n-drift`, `check:i18n-dead-keys`, `check:i18n-designer-parity`, `check-changeset-presence`, `check-changeset-no-major`, `check:changeset-claims`, `check:pending-changeset-literals`, `check:new-line-citations` (0 new), `check:vi-mock-specifiers`, `check:vi-mock-inherit`, `check:vi-mock-override-shape`, `check:test-path-roots`, `check:control-bytes`, `check:unreferenced-sources`, `check:spec-symbols`, `check:installed-pin-claims`, `check:doc-fences`, `check:doc-types`, `check:docs-route-closure`.
- ESLint on the 11 touched ts/tsx files: 0 errors. Compared with the same files on base, the one difference is one more `react-refresh/only-export-components` warning in `FlowReferenceField.tsx` (8 against 7), the same class as the file's existing exported helpers. The repo-wide lint run is CI's.
- NOT MEASURED: `check:readme-exports` and `check:doc-snippets`. Reason: their precondition is a built `dist` for every documented package, and neither was met here. Neither reads the two paragraphs this diff adds, because both gates read fenced code blocks and the paragraphs have none.

## Ablations (each leg on committed `61a2d3ed0`, mutation proven on disk, restored by `git checkout HEAD`, blob hash equal to HEAD, `git diff HEAD` empty)

| leg | mutation | went red |
|---|---|---|
| A1 | the designer's registry branch disabled | 5 tests: the select committing by name, the flagged stored name, the empty registry, the manual toggle, and the injected fallback render |
| A2 | `json-schema-to-fields` drops `registry` again | "keeps a published registry source, beside the record arm" |
| A3 | the spec-derived registry fallback returns nothing | "renders the registry select for a position with no published source" |
| A4 | the name arm forgets the registry | "prettifies a position approver instead of truncating it", "composes the registry label first…" |
| A5 | registry kinds no longer resolvable | "hands a server-unresolved position approver to the directory", "labels a position from the registry item…" |
| A6 | the hook's registry label leg skipped | "labels a position from the registry item, never from the sys_position mirror" |
| R1 | the hook's record label leg skipped | "keeps the record arm on the adapter" |
| R2 | the designer's record lookup disabled | "a published data source still renders the record lookup and lists no registry" |

## Acceptance notes

- The Approval Center inbox (`ApprovalsInboxPage`) already labels `position:` approvers from the registry, through its own `POSITION_REF_PREFIX` rather than the published binding. It reads correctly under both specs and is left as it is: routing it through the binding would drop its registry labels on the vendored console until spec 18. Carrier: none.
- On the vendored console the panel's label leg for a position still reads the `sys_position` mirror, so a fresh environment shows the prettified name (`Field Ops Delegate`) rather than the registry label (`Field Ops Delegate Admin`). The ruling leaves the record arm unchanged, and this goes away at spec 18. Carrier: none.
- On the vendored console, the designer's first render of an approval node, before the server schema arrives, still uses the record-lookup fallback, which costs two `sys_position` hydration reads. That fallback is the installed spec's binding and goes away at spec 18. Carrier: none.
